prompt: Write the body (about 120 words) of a letter of representation from a personal injury lawyer to an auto insurer. The client was hurt in a low-speed head-on collision. Ask that all contact go through the law firm, ask for the policy limits, and ask the insurer to keep all evidence. No salutation, no signature, no names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1194; do not mention it.)
text:
I am writing to advise that this office now represents the injured party in connection with the head-on collision described in your file. Please direct all further communication regarding this claim to our office and do not contact our client directly, whether by telephone, mail, or in person. Our client was injured in a low-speed impact and is undergoing medical evaluation, and we will forward supporting records as they become available.

Please provide a certified copy of the declarations page for the policy in force at the time of the accident, together with the stated bodily injury and property damage limits and a statement of any other coverage that may apply. We also ask that you confirm in writing whether any excess or umbrella coverage exists.

Finally, we request that your insurer preserve all evidence relating to this loss. This includes the claim file, photographs, vehicle data and event recorder information, telephone and recorded statements, repair and appraisal records, and any surveillance or third-party reports. Please treat this letter as a formal notice to preserve these materials, and confirm receipt so that we may proceed accordingly.
